claims.source: In fact, multiple conduction events across the open-dilated conformation of the triple-mutant chimera channel were observed in the simulation with the CHARMM36m force field, with no applied restraints.
claims.evidence: Observation from MD simulations in this study.

claims.claim: The structures of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m, Shaker-W434F, Kv1.2-W366F, and Shaker-lowK correspond to a conductive metastable intermediate on the path toward the true non-conductive C-type inactivated state.
claims.source: Based on our findings, we propose that the structures of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m (Reddi et al., 2022), Shaker-W434F (Tan et al., 2022), Kv1.2-W366F (Yangyu et al., 2024), and Shaker-lowK (Stix et al., 2023) corresponds to a conductive metastable intermediate on the path toward the true non-conductive C-type inactivated state wherein the permeation pathway is blocked by the isoleucine gate.
claims.evidence: Proposed model based on combined computational and experimental findings.

claims.claim: The free-energy landscape associated with C-type inactivation comprises two sequential transitions between three metastable states: conductive → dilated-intermediate → deeply inactivated.
claims.source: The free-energy landscape associated with the with C-type inactivation process comprises two sequential transitions between three metastable states: conductive → dilated-intermediate → deeply inactivated.
claims.evidence: Proposed model based on free-energy calculations shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: The transition from conductive to dilated state favors the dilated state with a downhill free-energy change of –12 kcal/mol.
claims.source: The first PMF monitoring the conformation of the selectivity filter while the isoleucine gate is in the open conformation shows two metastable states: conductive and dilated. The transition, which favors the latter state with a downhill free-energy change of –12 kcal/mol, involves a significant conformational change of Y373 from its buried configuration next to T367 in the conductive state toward its externally exposed orientation in the intermediate state resulting from unfavorable close interactions between the polar side chain of Y373 and F362.
claims.evidence: Free-energy calculation results shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: The transition from dilated-intermediate to deeply inactivated state shows a downhill change of –6.0 kcal/mol.
claims.source: As shown by the second PMF monitoring the closure of the isoleucine gate toward a non-conductive deep inactivated state while the filter remains in dilated conformation shows a downhill change of –6.0 kcal/mol.
claims.evidence: Free-energy calculation results shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: At +200 mV, the time constant of C-type inactivation is predicted to be in the same microsecond range of the simulated deep inactivation of the channel.
claims.source: Notwithstanding the limited accuracies of these computational estimates, the forward and backward free-energy barriers for these two transitions are in qualitative agreement with C-type inactivation of the triple-mutant channel in the sense that kv1.2-kv2.1-3m inactivates substantially faster than recovers from it—at +200 mV, the time constant of C-type inactivation is predicted to be in the same microsecond range of the simulated deep inactivation of the channel (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Comparison between free-energy calculations and experimental timescales shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: One or two Na+ ions can stably bind the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter at sites S3, S4, and Sext in the presence of 150 mM NaCl.
claims.source: AMBER and CHARM36m simulations of kv1.2-kv2.1-3m in presence of 150 mM NaCl show that one or two Na+ ions can stably bind the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter at sites S3, S4, and Sext, while favoring the open configuration of the isoleucine gate (Materials and methods, Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 1).
claims.evidence: MD simulation results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claims.claim: The internal [Na+]/[K+] concentration ratio seems to affect the closing of the isoleucine gate with functional implications for sodium leak in C-type inactivation.
claims.source: The internal [Na+]/[K+] concentration ratio seems to affect the closing of the isoleucine gate with functional implications for sodium leak in C-type inactivation.
claims.evidence: Inference from MD simulations with Na+ ions.

claims.claim: Most studied potassium channels including Kv1.2, Shaker-B, KcsA, and MthK display either isoleucine, leucine, valine, or phenylalanine at position 398.
claims.source: In particular, note that except for hERG, most studied potassium channels including, Kv1.2, Shaker-B, KcsA, and MthK, display either isoleucine, leucine, valine, or phenylalanine at position 398 (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).

claims.claim: The hERG channel has a tyrosine at position 398 which in the cryo-EM structure is twisted toward the central cavity in the open state.
claims.source: The hERG channel has a tyrosine at position 398 which in the cryo-EM structure (Wang and MacKinnon, 2017) is twisted toward the central cavity in the open state.

claims.claim: C-type inactivation in hERG might also involve constriction of the permeation pathway at position 398 when the selectivity filter is dilated.
claims.source: Because tyrosine is bulkier than asparagine, there is a chance that C-type inactivation in hERG also involves constriction of the permeation pathway at position 398 when the selectivity filter is dilated—another fascinating assumption worth of investigation in structural studies.
claims.evidence: Speculation based on structural comparison.

claims.claim: The isoleucine gate might interfere in a state-dependent manner with the mechanism of action of a broad class of QA blockers and negatively charged activators.
claims.source: As a piece of the molecular machinery implicated in multiple states, the isoleucine gate might interfere in a state-dependent manner with the mechanism of action of a broad class of QA blockers (Panyi and Deutsch, 2007) and negatively charged activators that bind beneath the selectivity filter and operate as master keys to open a variety of K+ channels (Schewe et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Speculation about broader implications, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The understanding of the isoleucine gate could offer a distinct advantage in the development of drugs that modulate gating states of potassium channels more specifically.
claims.source: Of particular importance, the understanding of this last aspect could offer a distinct advantage in the development of drugs that modulate gating states of potassium channels more specifically.
claims.evidence: Speculation about potential applications.

results.result: C-type inactivation is a well-established phenomenon in voltage-gated potassium channels involving conformational changes at the selectivity filter that transition from conductive to non-conductive states, contributing to long-term channel activity regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C9, and C10 represent established knowledge in the field, supported by multiple citations and consistent with the broader literature on Kv channel inactivation. These background claims provide the foundation for the current study.

results.result: Recent high-resolution structures of Kv channels revealed a dilated conformation of the selectivity filter that has been interpreted as the non-conductive C-type inactivated state.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C13, C14, and C15 accurately describe prior structural work (Reddi et al., 2022; Tan et al., 2022; Stix et al., 2023) that identified the dilated filter conformation and its interpretation. These are well-documented findings from the cited literature.

results.result: MD simulations using multiple force fields (AMBER, CHARMM36m, and CHARMM36m-NBFIX) demonstrate that the dilated conformation of the selectivity filter in kv1.2-kv2.1-3m is conductive, with estimated currents (~0.2 pA at +200 mV) orders of magnitude larger than experimentally measured inactivated currents.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C19-C21, C24, C26-C30, and C45 are well-supported by extensive MD simulation data shown in Figures 2 and supplementary figures. Multiple force fields converge on the conclusion that the dilated filter is conductive when the I398 gate is open. The quantitative estimates acknowledge force field limitations while demonstrating the key finding.

results.result: MD simulations reveal that isoleucine residues at position 398 form a hydrophobic gate that closes during simulations, constricting the permeation pathway beneath the selectivity filter and blocking ion conduction.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C6, C22, C23, and C46 are supported by detailed MD simulation data in Figure 2 showing the time-dependent closure of the I398 gate, with Cβ-Cβ distances decreasing from ~15 Å to ~9 Å, accompanied by dehydration and cessation of ion conduction. The structural and dynamic evidence is compelling.

results.result: Electrophysiological experiments show that the I398N mutation restores ion conduction in the triple-mutant channel without reverting C-type inactivation, as demonstrated by the lack of time-dependent inactivation and increased ionic current.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C31-C34 are supported by electrophysiological data in Figure 3 showing that I398N dramatically increases conductance in kv1.2-kv2.1-3m while maintaining the dilated filter conformation (as shown by toxin blocking experiments). The experimental evidence directly validates the computational predictions.

results.result: Toxin blocking experiments with AgTxII demonstrate that the I398N mutation does not stabilize the selectivity filter in the conductive state, indicating that ions conduct through the dilated filter and that the permeation pathway alteration occurs at I398 rather than the selectivity filter.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C34-C40 are supported by comprehensive toxin blocking experiments (Figure 3G-J) and computational binding free-energy calculations (Figure 3F). AgTxII blocks the conductive kv1.2-kv2.1 channel but not kv1.2-kv2.1-3m or kv1.2-kv2.1-3m_I398N, providing strong evidence that both maintain the dilated filter conformation.

results.result: Control experiments with the double mutant kv1.2-kv2.1-2m (lacking W362F) show that AgTxII blocks the channel regardless of I398N mutation, demonstrating that the I398N effect is specific to C-type inactivation.
results.evaluation: Claims C41 and C42 are supported by control experiments in Figure 3—figure supplement 3. The double mutant lacking the critical W362F mutation does not inactivate and is blocked by AgTxII with or without I398N, confirming the specificity of the I398 gate mechanism to C-type inactivation.

results.result: MD simulations of the I398N mutant show that the polar asparagine substitution keeps the permeation pathway constitutively hydrated and open, preventing gate closure.
results.evaluation: Claims C43, C44, and C48 are supported by MD simulation data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4 showing that I398N maintains an open, hydrated gate configuration. The mechanistic explanation is consistent with both computational and experimental observations.

results.result: Sequence conservation analysis shows that position 398 is occupied by hydrophobic residues (isoleucine, leucine, valine, or phenylalanine) in most studied potassium channels, suggesting the isoleucine gate is broadly relevant for C-type inactivation.
results.evaluation: Claims C47 and C67 are supported by sequence alignment data in Figure 3—figure supplement 5. The conservation of hydrophobic residues at position 398 across multiple K+ channels provides evidence for the general relevance of this gating mechanism.

results.result: Previous experimental observations in Shaker B channel showing that I470C mutations affect inactivation rates and QA blocker binding are consistent with the proposed I398 gate mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C52 appropriately cite and interpret prior experimental work (Holmgren et al., 1997; Olcese et al., 2001; Panyi and Deutsch, 2007) that is consistent with the current findings. The authors correctly connect historical observations to their new mechanistic model.

results.result: Free-energy calculations reveal a three-state model for C-type inactivation (conductive → dilated-intermediate → deeply inactivated) with sequential transitions showing downhill free-energy changes of -12 kcal/mol and -6 kcal/mol, with timescales consistent with experimental observations.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C64 are supported by PMF calculations shown in Figure 4. The free-energy landscape is qualitatively consistent with experimental kinetics (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), though the authors appropriately acknowledge computational limitations. The proposed three-state model integrates structural, computational, and experimental data.

results.result: Force field comparisons reveal that AMBER and CHARMM36m differ in their treatment of ion-carbonyl interactions, affecting ion binding at the selectivity filter and gate configuration, but both support the conclusion that the dilated filter is conductive when the I398 gate is open.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C59 provide important methodological context about force field limitations and differences. The authors appropriately acknowledge known issues with simulating ion conduction at physiological voltages and demonstrate that their main conclusions are robust across different force fields. The CHARMM36m-NBFIX validation strengthens the findings.

results.result: Structural analysis shows that the dilated and conductive conformations differ by ~3.0 Å RMSD, but the dilated filter remains accessible via a hydrated cavity with similar voltage drop across the selectivity filter.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C18 are supported by structural comparisons and electrostatic calculations shown in Figure 1. The quantitative structural analysis provides important context for understanding why the dilated conformation should be conductive.

results.result: The CHARMM36m force field favors the open configuration of the isoleucine gate.
results.evaluation: Claim C25 is supported by MD simulation observations showing that CHARMM36m maintains the I398 gate in an open configuration more readily than AMBER. This force field difference is important for interpreting the simulation results.

results.result: The isoleucine gate is expected to be coupled to the PVP motif, reflecting conformational allostery between the selectivity filter and bundle-crossing region.
results.evaluation: Claim C53 is supported by observations in the MD simulations (Figure 2) showing correlated motions between I398 and V402 (part of the PVP motif), consistent with prior literature on C-type inactivation allostery. The coupling is observed but not exhaustively characterized.

results.result: MD simulations in 150 mM NaCl show that Na+ ions can stably bind the dilated selectivity filter while favoring an open I398 gate configuration, suggesting that Na+/K+ concentration ratios may affect gate closure with implications for sodium leak during C-type inactivation.
results.evaluation: Claims C65 and C66 are based on preliminary MD simulations (Figure 4—figure supplement 3) showing Na+ binding to the dilated filter. While the observations are interesting, the functional implications for sodium leak are speculative and would require additional experimental validation. The connection to physiological sodium leak is not firmly established.

results.result: The hERG channel has a tyrosine at position 398, and C-type inactivation in hERG might involve constriction at this position when the selectivity filter is dilated.
results.evaluation: Claims C68 and C69 are based on structural observations from cited work (Wang and MacKinnon, 2017) and speculation about hERG inactivation. While the structural observation is accurate, the proposed mechanism for hERG is explicitly acknowledged as speculative and requires experimental investigation.

results.result: The isoleucine gate might interfere with QA blockers and negatively charged activators in a state-dependent manner, potentially offering advantages for drug development targeting specific gating states.
results.evaluation: Claims C70 and C71 are speculative proposals about potential drug development applications. While the mechanistic insights about the I398 gate are well-supported, the specific implications for drug design are hypothetical and would require extensive follow-up work.

results.result: The canonical conductive state of the K+ channel selectivity filter was first revealed by KcsA crystal structures, and MD studies confirm ion conduction is possible without large free-energy barriers.
results.evaluation: Claims C11 and C12 accurately cite foundational structural and computational work on K+ channel selectivity filters. These are well-established findings that provide appropriate background context.
